family.description: This family includes a range of acyltransferase enzymes. This domain is found in a wide range of acyltransferase enzymes, including, mainly, bacterial proteins which catalyse the transfer of acyl groups, other than amino-acyl, from one compound to another, such as Glucans biosynthesis protein C (OPGC) or protein OatA from Listeria monocytogenes serovar 1/2a and Staphylococcus aureus, an integral membrane protein which is responsible for O-acetylation at the C6-hydroxyl group of N-acetylmuramyl residues, forming the corresponding N,6-O-diacetylmuramic acid of the peptidoglycan, a modification that determines lysozyme resistance [[cite:PUB00097284],[cite:PUB00097283]]. This domain is also present in eukaryotic proteins, namely O-acyltransferase like protein (OACYL) from mouse and RHY1 (Regulator of hypoxia-inducible factor 1) [[cite:PUB00097285]] and NRF6 (Nose resistant to fluoxetine protein 6) from Caenorhabditis elegans [[cite:PUB00097286]].
family.name: Acyltransferase domain

causal_graphs.family_mapping: 603-aa Q2FV54/NCTC8325 and A0A0H2XFE4/USA300 references are identical to versioned ABD21303.1; PF01757 19-344. WT MS searches use Q2FV54, not a resequenced clone. S453 and the isolated C-domain 445-601 are outside current PF01757. Full-length clone donor strain/termini require SI verification.
causal_graphs.limitations: DIRECT describes net purified-preparation effects, not isolated-domain sufficiency. The MS S453A search reference also has K495A/K496A and LE+His10; whether the Figure1 preparation shared those changes is unresolved. Treat it as the published S453A preparation, not an independently verified single mutant. The C-domain negative comparator is plotted only for GM-penta. No atomic relay, exact acceptor bond or calibrated product yield is inferred from these spectra.

causal_graphs.context: Proposed membrane-associated donor acquisition from acetyl-CoA, followed by intramolecular transfer from an acetylated Tyr206 to the cognate C-terminal Ser453. Full-length OatA supplies both sites; these are joint protein/substrate states, not independently sufficient residues.

evidence.explanation: Figure5B and Discussion explicitly propose the catalytic triad; MS deposit limitations are retained in the paired evidence ledger.
Limitation on causal attribution, not positive relay proof; both treated and untreated search outputs identify acetylated Tyr206, and the search reference includes additional lysine substitutions.

edges.mechanism: The authors propose H36/E154-assisted activation of Tyr206 to acquire acetyl from acetyl-CoA. Mutation phenotypes and modified peptides motivate this hypothesis but do not observe its acid-base steps or identify the origin of each detected acetyl group.
edges.subject: donor-and-unmodified-oata

evidence.explanation: Trapping Results, Figure4 partner-domain assay and Discussion; Figure4E caption18 h versus Results2 h remains unresolved.

edges.mechanism: The proposed intramolecular relay passes acetyl from Tyr206 to C-domain Ser453. Separate acetyl-peptide detections and synthetic-donor assays are compatible with this model but do not directly track this transfer or exclude alternative paths.
edges.subject: tyr206-acetylated-oata

causal_graphs.family_mapping: PF01757 19-344 in the matched Q2FV54/A0A0H2XFE4/ABD21303.1 references includes H36,E154,Y206 but excludes S453 and the isolated445-601 partner. E357 is also outside current PF01757 and must not be confused with proposed E154. Topology-library ATCC6538 and purified-clone provenance remain distinct.
causal_graphs.limitations: Both edges are HYPOTHESIZED and directness UNRESOLVED. Deposited treated and untreated S453A samples both contain acetylated Tyr206; the search reference includes K495A/K496A. This is not treatment-specific flux proof. Synthetic acetyl-Tyr donor use by isolated C-domain does not observe an intramolecular relay. No atomic OatA structure or proton-transfer trajectory is established by Figure5; OafB modelling is not SaOatA experimental validation.
